title: Preserve useful review work with permissive progress-based timeouts
userValue: Slow but progressing reviews survive remote model/network delays and local machine load without wasting completed model work.
scope: Replace size-based 5/10/15-minute hard review cutoffs with expected-duration reporting and permissive progress monitoring.
Use observable model output, tool starts/completions and submitted feedback as progress signals; distinguish a live process from meaningful progress.
Track long-running tools separately with appropriate limits so hung commands cannot keep a review alive forever.
Represent remote waiting with unknown progress honestly; allow generous inactivity grace and record diagnostics before intervention.
Capture and validate complete submitted feedback durably before process termination; recover available results before considering another attempt.
Keep controller-triggered subsequent attempts, per-task checkpoints, independent review and identical Claude/Codex behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: Active but slow reviews are not killed merely because a size-based expected duration elapsed.
Remote silence, ongoing tool execution, local contention, tool hangs and genuine inactivity have distinguishable diagnostics and tested intervention behavior.
A complete valid assessment submitted near termination can be retained without rerunning the model or accepting unvalidated transcript content.
No automatic whole-review retries or repeated completed tasks; incomplete work stays explicit.
Both supported CLI providers preserve the same policy and approval safeguards.
evidence: Review review-e6ddcdcb3d9cf330-s1-final: Task4 submitted StructuredOutput at 16:35:48 UTC, but its 600000ms host deadline elapsed before the final CLI envelope returned.
openDesignDecisions: Meaningful progress signals, grace periods and per-tool limits across Claude/Codex.
Safe early-feedback capture and validation without treating transcript/tool acknowledgements as completed host results.
currentWork: Backlog only. Continue existing S1 code-review findings; do not implement this policy change in S1.
